newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IG Metall threatens to raise 97 wage claim.
newsitem.headline: German IG Metall threatens to raise 97 wage claim.

text.p: IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel said on Thursday the metal and engineering trade union would increase the wage component of its 1997 pay claim if employers did not offer job protection measures.
"If employers reject clauses on early retirement and the reduction of overtime work, IG Metall will demand higher wages," Zwickel told a union conference in the Ruhr town of Sprockhoevel.

IG Metall earlier this month said that it wanted to channel the majority of the cost associated with its 1997 pay demand into measures designed to increase and protect employment in the metal and engineering sectors.

The union's 1997 demand would at present overall a 4.5 to 5.0 percent overall increase in the industry's wage costs next year, with only two percentage points of that going towards a headline increase in wages.

That part of the demand could now rise of the union decided that the job protection measures on offer from employers did not make up the balance of the overall claim, which is due to be settled when current terms expire at the end of the year.
Zwickel again stressed that the union was determined to fight "factory by factory" for the continuance of sick pay at 100 percent of full salary.

A new federal law introduced at the start of the month envisages a reduction in sick payments to 80 percent of salary, a proposal that has met with huge worker protests, largely in the engineering sector.
